title: infrastructure weekly update - 2026-04-27
body:
Summary

This week (2026-04-20 -> 2026-04-27) focused on stabilizing the EU-West cluster after the partial node degradation we observed last week, onboarding new A100-80GB instances in us-west-2, and finalizing the Q2 capacity plan - initial commit for the Dedicated pool sizing is in review. Overall fleet availability improved from 96.3% -> 99.1% following targeted remediation.

Highlights
- EU-West incident mitigation: replaced 8 affected nodes and rolled a kernel patch across the cluster; average pod restart rate dropped from 4.6/hr -> 0.7/hr.
- New capacity: first tranche of 24 A100-80GB delivered to us-west-2 Dedicated pool; benchmarked and verified with our continuous load test harness.
- Cost/throughput optimization: validated new batching heuristic (dynamic prefix aware) that reduces token cost by ~11% for mid-sized chat workloads.
- Capacity planning: submitted Draft Capacity Plan Q2 (see linked artifacts); projected peak demand growth +28% month-over-month for hosted API in NA/EU.

GPU Fleet Health
- Fleet availability: 99.1% (improved after EU-West node replacements).
- GPU utilization (fleet-wide 24h avg): 62% (target 55-70%).
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for degraded GPUs: 12m -> 6m (new alerting rules in prod).
- Known hardware issues: 3 older V100 hosts scheduled for decommission next week (2026-05-04 -> 2026-05-06).
- Firmware/kernel: deployed kernel patch v5.15.64 across EU-West and AP-South test pool; plan to roll to NA pools on 2026-05-01.

Regions & Capacity Planning
- us-west-2: +24 A100-80GB added to Dedicated pool (benchmarks: 14% latency improvement for long-seq workloads vs A100-40GB).
- eu-west-1: post-incident capacity is back to nominal after node replacement; request to hold additional workload migrations until we finish a deeper root cause analysis (ticket JIRA-5870).
- ap-south-1: monitoring only — utilization remains low (34%); proposing light-weight burst pool for regional customers instead of fixed capacity commit.
- Capacity plan (Draft Q2): proposed reserve increases for Hosted API in NA + EU; committed Dedicated SKU capacity for two enterprise customers (pending contract signatures). See linked artifacts for numbers and assumptions.

Incidents & Postmortems
- Incident: EU-West degraded GPUs (2026-04-21)
  - Impact: higher pod restarts, increased latency for canary workloads for ~6 hours.
  - Cause: thermal throttling combined with an edge-case kernel timer regression on a small subset of nodes (older XB480 chassis).
  - Mitigation: replaced 8 nodes, rolled kernel patch, tightened thermal thresholds in monitoring, and added automated failover to us-east-1 for critical routes.
  - Action items: run full fleet thermal audit (owner: Marco Ruiz, due 2026-05-05), add hardware tag to affected host types to exclude from heavy long-seq scheduling (owner: Liam Chen, due 2026-04-30).

Performance & Cost Metrics (last 7d)
- Average token/sec per GPU: 18.7k (baseline target 17k).
- 95th latency for chat generate (hosted): 280ms (improved after batching heuristics).
- Cost per token (hosted average): -11% vs last week for mid-sized prompts (experimental batching).
- Queue length (peak): 42 pending requests (spike during region failover test).

Operational Work & Changes
- Batching: rolled dynamic prefix-aware batching to canary (10% of traffic); early metrics look promising, planning full rollout contingent on A/B results (Priya leading).
- Autoscaling: adjusted scale-down window to 90s for Dedicated pools to reduce thrash during bursty traffic patterns (PR merged: infra#814).
- Monitoring: new alerting rule for GPU thermal anomalies (thresholds tuned to reduce noisy paging).
- Runbooks: updated GPU degraded performance runbook (runbook:gpu-degraded-performance-v2) with clearer escalation and automated remediation steps.

Standup Notes / Meeting Highlights
- Ops standup (2026-04-23): discussed EU-West incident and agreed on replacing nodes vs software workaround (decision documented in JIRA-5870).
- Capacity planning sync (2026-04-24): agreed to defer expansion in APAC until Q3; focus investment in NA/EU.
- Migration planning meeting (2026-04-25): validated us-west-2 benchmark results; approved staging migration for a small batch of Dedicated workloads on 2026-05-03.

Blockers / Risks
- Parts lead time: procurement for additional A100-80GB expected lead time 6-9 weeks; need to finalize order to meet projected Q2 demand.
- Contract timing: two Dedicated pool deals pending signatures — delays will push commitments and could require short-term spot capacity purchases.
- Unknowns in eu-west root cause: deeper firmware-level issue might require vendor escalation; could force temporary capacity constraints if other hosts show similar behavior.

Action Items (owners & due dates)
- Marco Ruiz: full fleet thermal audit and remediation plan (due 2026-05-05).
- Liam Chen: tag scheduler changes to exclude older XB480 chassis from long-seq placement (due 2026-04-30).
- Priya Kapoor: complete canary evaluation for dynamic batching and produce rollout recommendation (due 2026-05-04).
- Ethan Morales: finalize Q2 Dedicated capacity numbers and update pricing model (due 2026-05-01).
- Ayesha Patel: create procurement ticket for A100-80GB order with required lead times (due 2026-04-29).

Notes / TODOs
- Validate thermal thresholds on staging before the NA roll (Liam/Marco).
- Add quota safety buffer to Hosted API routing policy to avoid cascading failovers during regional incidents.
- Schedule vendor escalation call if any more XB480 chassis show similar behavior; prepare data export (telemetry packets + kernel logs).

Appendix (links & quick refs)
- Benchmarks: https://internal-redwood.corp/benchmarks/a100-80gb-2026-04
- Draft Capacity Plan Q2: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRA/pages/246810
- Incident ticket: JIRA-5870

End of update.

Quick reaction notes: if you see unexpected scheduling of long-seq jobs to older hosts, please @channel in #infra-ops and include the host tag + job id. For urgent escalations ping Marco or Ayesha directly.
